THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This is claimant's appeal for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge &
JMFC and Additional MACT-IV, Shahapur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for short) in MVC No.195/2016 dated 17.01.2022.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3768
Though this appeal is stated for orders, with the consent of both the side, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the appellant- claimant met with an accident on 27.08.2015 at Halisagar of Shahapur taluka, due to rash and negligent driving of tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-32/B-9197 by its driver.
As a result of which, petitioner sustained fracture of both bones of right leg and other injuries.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, he has been suffering from permanent disability.

With these reasons, the claimant prayed to award compensation of Ambanna @ Ambalappa vs Preetam T Mehta And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57894568/
2 Rs.12,75,000/-.
4.

From the rival contentions of both the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues for its determination.
6. The claimant to prove his case examined PWs.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.P1 to 15 and closed his evidence.
Respondents have not led any evidence.
7. After hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record, the Tribunal by its impugned judgment, awarded the following amount of compensation.

 NC: 2024:KHC-K:3768 8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and respondent No.2.
9. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Therefore, prayed for enhancement of compensation.
10. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and submitted that there are no grounds to interfere with the findings of the Tribunal.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
11. The following question arises for determination.

sentences.text: "Whether the claimant is entitled for the enhancement of compensation?
12. I have gone through the impugned judgment; The fact of the accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, his age as well as income assessed by the Tribunal are not in serious dispute.

Therefore,
there is no need to reconsider the same.

The Tribunal had awarded NC: 2024:KHC-K:3768 lesser amount of compensation under the head of loss of amenities, attendant charges, special diet,
conveyance charges, etc, which needs to be enhanced.
13. Considering these facts and circumstances, global compensation of Rs.25,000/- is enhanced in addition to the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, I answered the above question partly in the affirmative and pass following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC and Addl. MACT-IV, Shahapur, in MVC.No.195/2016 dated 17.01.2022 is modified;
(a) A sum of Rs.25,000/- is enhanced globally in addition to the amount awarded by the Tribunal, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced NC:
2024:KHC-K:3768 amount of compensation from the date of petition till its realization.
iii. Respondent No.2 - insurance company shall deposit the said amount with interest before the Tribunal within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
iv. Amount of compensation enhanced is meager and hence entire enhanced amount with interest is ordered to be released in favour of claimant on due identification.

Sd/- 
JUDGE SDU CT:PK Ambanna @ Ambalappa vs Preetam T Mehta And Anr
